model_annotation: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 1 to 3000 with major ticks shown at 0, 10, 100, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 37% to 67% with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38% at co-occurrence 3 to about 42% at 30, then to about 44% at 300 and remaining about 44% at 3000. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 40% (3) to about 43% (30), about 46% (300), and about 48% (3000). IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, moving from about 43% (3) to about 45% (30), about 46.5% (300), and about 49.5% (3000). MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 44.5% (3) to about 49% (30), about 54% (300), and about 56.5% (3000). MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, rising from about 44% (3) to about 51% (30), about 53% (300), and about 55% (3000). ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51% (3) to about 57% (30), about 62.5% (300), and about 66% (3000).
